# Book III, Proposition 15

*Of straight lines in a circle the diameter is greatest*

> Of straight lines in a circle the diameter is greatest, and of the rest the nearer to the centre is always greater than the more remote.

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/III/15-idea.svg" alt="Of all the straight lines in a circle the diameter (red) is the greatest, and of the rest the one nearer the centre (blue) is greater than the one farther off (yellow)." width="420"></p>

<p align="center"><em>Of all the straight lines in a circle the diameter (red) is the greatest, and of the rest the one nearer the centre (blue) is greater than the one farther off (yellow).</em></p>

## Euclid's proof

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/III/15.svg" alt="Euclid's figure for Proposition III.15, with Heath's letters" width="360"></p>

Let ABCD be a circle, let AD be its diameter and E the centre; and let BC be nearer to the diameter AD, and FG more remote;

I say that AD is greatest and BC greater than FG.

For from the centre E let EH, EK be drawn perpendicular to BC, FG.

Then, since BC is nearer to the centre and FG more remote, EK is greater than EH. [III. Def. 5]

Let EL be made equal to EH, through L let LM be drawn at right angles to EK and carried through to N, and let ME, EN, FE, EG be joined.

Then, since EH is equal to EL,

BC is also equal to MN. [III. 14]

Again, since AE is equal to EM, and ED to EN,

AD is equal to ME, EN.

But ME, EN are greater than MN, [I. 20]

and MN is equal to BC;

therefore AD is greater than BC.

And, since the two sides ME, EN are equal to the two sides FE, EG,

and the angle MEN greater than the angle FEG,

therefore the base MN is greater than the base FG. [I. 24]

But MN was proved equal to BC.

Therefore the diameter AD is greatest and BC greater than FG.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.

From [`Elements/BookIII/Prop15.lean`](../../Elements/BookIII/Prop15.lean). Euclid's sentences are the `--` comments, and our own notes are in `/- … -/`; the lines under each sentence are the Lean that carries it out.

```lean
/-- Half of "the angle MEN greater than the angle FEG": where `MN` cuts `EF` at `X`, `X`
is within the circle and on `M`'s side of `EK`, so it lies between `M` and `L`, and the
angle `FEK` (which is `XEL`) is a part of `MEL`. -/
theorem Prop15.half {E F K L M : Point} {α : Circle} {EK MN : Line}
    (hE : Centre E α) (hF : OnCircle F α) (hM : OnCircle M α)
    (hE_EK : OnLine E EK) (hL_EK : OnLine L EK) (hELK : Between E L K)
    (hL_MN : OnLine L MN) (hM_MN : OnLine M MN) (hE_MN : ¬ OnLine E MN)
    (hL_in : InsideCircle L α) (hEF : OppositeSides E F MN)
    (hMF : SameSide M F EK) (hF_EK : ¬ OnLine F EK) :
    ∠ F E K < ∠ M E L := by
  obtain ⟨X, hX_MN, hEXF⟩ := hEF.exists_between
  have hX_in : InsideCircle X α := inside_of_between (Or.inl (centre_inside hE)) (Or.inr hF) hEXF
  have hX_EK : ¬ OnLine X EK := fun h => hF_EK (on_line_of_between hEXF hE_EK h)
  have hXF : SameSide X F EK := pasch2 hEXF hE_EK hX_EK
  have hXM : SameSide X M EK := same_side_trans (same_side_symm hXF) (same_side_symm hMF)
  have hMX : M ≠ X := fun e => inside_not_on hX_in (e ▸ hM)
  have hXL : X ≠ L := fun e => hX_EK (e ▸ hL_EK)
  have hML : M ≠ L := fun e => not_on_line_of_same_side hMF (e ▸ hL_EK)
  have hMXL : Between M X L := by
    rcases between_cases hMX hXL hML hM_MN hX_MN hL_MN with h | h | h
    · exact h
    · exact absurd hM (inside_not_on (inside_of_between (Or.inl hX_in) (Or.inl hL_in) h))
    · exact absurd (same_side_symm hXM) (pasch3 h hL_EK)
  have hMLE : Triangle M L E := Triangle.of_line hM_MN hL_MN hML hE_MN
  rw [← angle_eq_of_onRay (OnRay.of_between hEXF) (OnRay.of_between hELK)]
  exact angle_lt_of_between hMLE hMXL

/-- When `M`, `L`, `N` lie in that order and `ELM` is right, `EL` makes a right
angle with every ray of `MN` issuing from `L`. Euclid carries `LM` through to `N`
and uses this perpendicular to compare distances from the centre. -/
theorem Prop15.perp {E L M N : Point} {MN : Line} (hM_MN : OnLine M MN) (hN_MN : OnLine N MN)
    (hMLN : Between M L N) (hE_MN : ¬ OnLine E MN) (hELM : ∠ E L M = ∟) :
    ∀ P : Point, Collinear M N P → P ≠ L → ∠ E L P = ∟ := by
  have hEL : E ≠ L := fun e => hE_MN (e ▸ on_line_of_between_ends hMLN hM_MN hN_MN)
  have hML : M ≠ L := ne_of_between hMLN
  have hMLE : ∠ M L E = ∟ := (angle_symm hML hEL).trans hELM
  have hELN : ∠ E L N = ∟ := (adjacent_eq_of_right hM_MN hN_MN hMLN hE_MN hMLE).symm.trans hMLE
  intro P hP hPL
  obtain ⟨ν, hM_ν, hN_ν, hP_ν⟩ := hP
  rw [line_unique (ne_of_between_ends hMLN) hM_ν hN_ν hM_MN hN_MN] at hP_ν
  rcases OnRay.cases_of_between hMLN hM_MN hN_MN hP_ν hPL with h | h
  · exact (angle_onRay_right h hEL).trans hELM
  · exact (angle_onRay_right h hEL).trans hELN

/-- Of straight lines in a circle the diameter is greatest, and of the rest the nearer to the centre
is always greater than the more remote. -/
theorem Prop15 {A B C D E F G H K : Point} {ABCD : Circle} (hE : Centre E ABCD)
    (hA : OnCircle A ABCD) (hD : OnCircle D ABCD) (hAED : Between A E D)
    (hB : OnCircle B ABCD) (hC : OnCircle C ABCD) (hF : OnCircle F ABCD)
    (hG : OnCircle G ABCD) (hE_BC : ¬ Collinear B C E) (hE_FG : ¬ Collinear F G E)
    (hH : Collinear B C H) (hEH : ∀ P : Point, Collinear B C P → P ≠ H → ∠ E H P = ∟)
    (hK : Collinear F G K) (hEK : ∀ P : Point, Collinear F G P → P ≠ K → ∠ E K P = ∟)
    (hnearer : ‖E H‖ < ‖E K‖) :
    ‖B C‖ < ‖A D‖ ∧ ‖F G‖ < ‖B C‖ := by
  -- Let ABCD be a circle, let AD be its diameter and E the centre; and let BC be nearer to the
  -- diameter AD, and FG more remote;
  -- I say that AD is greatest and BC greater than FG.
  -- For from the centre E let EH, EK be drawn perpendicular to BC, FG.
  /- Given; the foot K falls between F and G [I. 17, I. 19, through `foot_between`]. -/
  have hFKG : Between F K G := foot_between hE hF hG hE_FG hK hEK
  -- Then, since BC is nearer to the centre and FG more remote, EK is greater than
  -- EH. [III. Def. 5]
  /- Given, as `hnearer`. -/
  -- Let EL be made equal to EH, through L let LM be drawn at right angles to EK and carried
  -- through to N, and let ME, EN, FE, EG be joined.
  /- Cut EL off EK [I. 3]. -/
  have hEH' : E ≠ H := fun e => hE_BC (e ▸ hH)
  obtain ⟨L, hELK, hEL⟩ := BookI.Prop3 hEH' hnearer
  have hEK' : E ≠ K := ne_of_between_ends hELK
  obtain ⟨EK, hE_EK, hK_EK⟩ := Postulate1 E K hEK'
  have hL_EK : OnLine L EK := on_line_of_between_ends hELK hE_EK hK_EK
  obtain ⟨FG, hF_FG, hG_FG⟩ := Postulate1 F G (ne_of_between_ends hFKG)
  have hK_FG : OnLine K FG := on_line_of_between_ends hFKG hF_FG hG_FG
  have hE_FG_line : ¬ OnLine E FG := fun h => hE_FG ⟨FG, hF_FG, hG_FG, h⟩
  have hF_EK : ¬ OnLine F EK := fun h =>
    hE_FG_line (line_unique (ne_of_between hFKG) h hK_EK hF_FG hK_FG ▸ hE_EK)
  have hG_EK : ¬ OnLine G EK := fun h =>
    hE_FG_line (line_unique (ne_of_between (between_symm hFKG)) h hK_EK hG_FG hK_FG ▸ hE_EK)
  /- Draw LM at right angles to EK [I. 11], on F's side. -/
  obtain ⟨R, hRF, hR⟩ := BookI.Prop11 hEK' ⟨EK, hE_EK, hK_EK, hL_EK⟩
    (fun ⟨l, h1, h2, h3⟩ => hF_EK (line_unique hEK' h1 h2 hE_EK hK_EK ▸ h3))
  have hR_EK : ¬ OnLine R EK := not_on_line_of_same_side (hRF.sameSide hE_EK hK_EK)
  have hRL : R ≠ L := fun e => hR_EK (e ▸ hL_EK)
  obtain ⟨MN, hL_MN, hR_MN⟩ := Postulate1 L R hRL.symm
  /- Carry it through to N; L is within the circle. -/
  have hK_in : InsideCircle K ABCD := inside_of_between (Or.inr hF) (Or.inr hG) hFKG
  have hL_in : InsideCircle L ABCD :=
    inside_of_between (Or.inl (centre_inside hE)) (Or.inl hK_in) hELK
  obtain ⟨N, hN, hN_MN, hNLR⟩ := line_circle_beyond hL_in hL_MN hR_MN hRL
  obtain ⟨M, hM, hM_MN, hMLN⟩ := line_circle_beyond hL_in hL_MN hN_MN (ne_of_between hNLR)
  /- `MN` meets `EK` at `L` alone. -/
  have only_L : ∀ P, OnLine P MN → OnLine P EK → P = L := fun P hPMN hPEK =>
    Classical.byContradiction fun hPL => hR_EK (line_unique hPL hPMN hL_MN hPEK hL_EK ▸ hR_MN)
  have hE_MN_line : ¬ OnLine E MN := fun h => (ne_of_between hELK) (only_L E h hE_EK)
  have hK_MN : ¬ OnLine K MN := fun h => (ne_of_between (between_symm hELK)) (only_L K h hK_EK)
  have hM_EK : ¬ OnLine M EK := fun h => (ne_of_between hMLN) (only_L M hM_MN h)
  have hN_EK : ¬ OnLine N EK := fun h => (ne_of_between (between_symm hMLN)) (only_L N hN_MN h)
  /- `M` on `F`'s side of `EK`, `N` on `G`'s. -/
  have hNR : OppositeSides N R EK := ⟨hN_EK, hR_EK, pasch3 hNLR hL_EK⟩
  have hNM : OppositeSides N M EK := ⟨hN_EK, hM_EK, pasch3 (between_symm hMLN) hL_EK⟩
  have hMF : SameSide M F EK :=
    same_side_trans (same_side_of_opposite_sides hNR hNM) (hRF.sameSide hE_EK hK_EK)
  have hFG : OppositeSides F G EK := ⟨hF_EK, hG_EK, pasch3 hFKG hK_EK⟩
  have hFN : OppositeSides F N EK :=
    ⟨hF_EK, hN_EK, fun h => hNR.2.2 (same_side_trans h (same_side_symm (hRF.sameSide hE_EK hK_EK)))⟩
  have hNG : SameSide N G EK := same_side_of_opposite_sides hFN hFG
  /- The perpendicular makes right angles with both rays of MN from L. -/
  have hMLR : OnRay M L R := OnRay.of_between_between hNLR (between_symm hMLN)
  have hELM : ∠ E L M = ∟ :=
    (angle_onRay_right hMLR (ne_of_between hELK)).trans
      (hR E ⟨EK, hE_EK, hK_EK, hE_EK⟩ (ne_of_between hELK))
  have hEL_perp := Prop15.perp hM_MN hN_MN hMLN hE_MN_line hELM
  /- Joining ME and EN makes the triangle MEN. -/
  have hE_MN : ¬ Collinear M N E := fun ⟨l, h1, h2, h3⟩ =>
    hE_MN_line (line_unique (ne_of_between_ends hMLN) h1 h2 hM_MN hN_MN ▸ h3)
  have hL : Collinear M N L := ⟨MN, hM_MN, hN_MN, hL_MN⟩
  -- Then, since EH is equal to EL,
  have hEH_EL : ‖E H‖ = ‖E L‖ := hEL.symm
  -- BC is also equal to MN. [III. 14]
  have hBC_MN : ‖B C‖ = ‖M N‖ :=
    (Prop14 hE hB hC hM hN hE_BC hE_MN hH hEH hL hEL_perp).2 hEH_EL
  -- Again, since AE is equal to EM, and ED to EN,
  have hAE : ‖A E‖ = ‖E M‖ := (len_symm A E).trans (Definition15 hE hA hM)
  have hED : ‖E D‖ = ‖E N‖ := Definition15 hE hD hN
  -- AD is equal to ME, EN.
  have hAD : ‖A D‖ = ‖M E‖ + ‖E N‖ := by
    rw [← len_add_of_between hAED, hAE, hED, len_symm M E]
  -- But ME, EN are greater than MN, [I. 20]
  have h20 : ‖M N‖ < ‖M E‖ + ‖E N‖ := (BookI.Prop20 (Triangle.cab hE_MN)).1
  -- and MN is equal to BC;
  rw [← hBC_MN] at h20
  -- therefore AD is greater than BC.
  have hdiameter : ‖B C‖ < ‖A D‖ := by
    rw [hAD]
    exact h20
  -- And, since the two sides ME, EN are equal to the two sides FE, EG,
  have hEM : ‖E M‖ = ‖E F‖ := Definition15 hE hM hF
  have hEN : ‖E N‖ = ‖E G‖ := Definition15 hE hN hG
  -- and the angle MEN greater than the angle FEG,
  /- `FG` and `MN` never meet: at a common point `Z` the triangle `ZLK` would have two
     right angles [I. 17]. So `F` and `G` are on `K`'s side of `MN`, and `E` on the other. -/
  have par : Parallel FG MN := Parallel.of_not_meet hF_FG fun Z hZFG hZMN => by
    have hZL : Z ≠ L := by
      intro e
      have hFG_EK := line_unique (ne_of_between (between_symm hELK)).symm
        (e ▸ hZFG) hK_FG hL_EK hK_EK
      exact hE_FG_line (hFG_EK ▸ hE_EK)
    have hZ_EK : ¬ OnLine Z EK := fun h => hZL (only_L Z hZMN h)
    have hZK : Z ≠ K := fun e => hZ_EK (e ▸ hK_EK)
    have hELZ : ∠ E L Z = ∟ := hEL_perp Z ⟨MN, hM_MN, hN_MN, hZMN⟩ hZL
    have hZLK : ∠ Z L K = ∟ := by
      have h := adjacent_eq_of_right hE_EK hK_EK hELK hZ_EK hELZ
      exact h.symm.trans hELZ
    have hLKZ : ∠ L K Z = ∟ := by
      have hEKZ : ∠ E K Z = ∟ := hEK Z ⟨FG, hF_FG, hG_FG, hZFG⟩ hZK
      rw [angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between (between_symm hELK)) hZK]
      exact hEKZ
    have hZLK' : Triangle Z L K :=
      (Triangle.of_line hL_EK hK_EK (ne_of_between (between_symm hELK)).symm hZ_EK).cab
    have h17 := (BookI.Prop17 hZLK').1
    rw [hZLK, hLKZ] at h17
    exact lt_irrefl _ h17
  have hEK_MN : OppositeSides E K MN := ⟨hE_MN_line, hK_MN, pasch3 hELK hL_MN⟩
  have hEF_MN : OppositeSides E F MN :=
    ⟨hE_MN_line, par.not_onLine hF_FG, fun h => hEK_MN.2.2 (same_side_trans (same_side_symm h)
      (par.sameSide hF_FG hK_FG))⟩
  have hEG_MN : OppositeSides E G MN :=
    ⟨hE_MN_line, par.not_onLine hG_FG, fun h => hEK_MN.2.2 (same_side_trans (same_side_symm h)
      (par.sameSide hG_FG hK_FG))⟩
  have h1 : ∠ F E K < ∠ M E L :=
    Prop15.half hE hF hM hE_EK hL_EK hELK hL_MN hM_MN hE_MN_line hL_in hEF_MN hMF hF_EK
  have h2 : ∠ G E K < ∠ N E L :=
    Prop15.half hE hG hN hE_EK hL_EK hELK hL_MN hN_MN hE_MN_line hL_in hEG_MN hNG hG_EK
  have hMEN : ∠ F E G < ∠ M E N := by
    rw [angle_add_of_between hE_FG hFKG, angle_add_of_between hE_MN hMLN,
      angle_symm hEK'.symm (fun e : G = E => hG_EK (e ▸ hE_EK)),
      angle_symm (ne_of_between hELK).symm (fun e : N = E => hN_EK (e ▸ hE_EK))]
    exact lt_trans (add_lt_add_right _ h1) (by
      rw [add_comm (∠ M E L), add_comm (∠ M E L)]; exact add_lt_add_right _ h2)
  -- therefore the base MN is greater than the base FG. [I. 24]
  have h24 : ‖F G‖ < ‖M N‖ := BookI.Prop24 (Triangle.cab hE_MN) (Triangle.cab hE_FG) hEM hEN hMEN
  -- But MN was proved equal to BC.
  rw [← hBC_MN] at h24
  -- Therefore the diameter AD is greatest and BC greater than FG.
  exact ⟨hdiameter, h24⟩
  -- Therefore etc.
  -- Q. E. D.
```

- [`between_cases`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L74) (used here): Of three different points on a straight line, one is between the other two. (Between 6)
- [`between_of_between_left`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L66): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, and `D` is between `A` and `B`, then `D` is between `A` and `C`. (Between 4)
- [`between_of_between_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L70): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, and `C` is between `B` and `D`, then `B` is between `A` and `D`. (Between 5)
- [`between_of_inside_chord`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L155) (used here): A straight line through a point inside a circle has that point between the points where it meets the circle. (Circle 1)
- [`between_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L43) (used here): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, it is between `C` and `A`. (Between 1)
- [`centre_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L35) (used here): The centre of a circle is inside it. (Generalities 3)
- [`centre_unique`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L32): A circle has only one centre. (Generalities 2)
- [`circles_meet`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L201): If each circle passes through a point inside the other, the circles cut one another. This is the step Euclid takes for granted in I.1. (Intersection 5)
- [`circles_meet_of_on_inside_outside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L195): Two circles cut one another if the first passes through a point `A` inside the second, and a point `B` outside the second is inside or on the first. (Intersection 4, in LeanEuclid's corrected form)
- [`circles_meet_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L81): Two circles that cut one another do so on each side of the straight line through their centres. (Intersections 8)
- [`exists_point`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L26) (used here): Let a point be taken. (Points 1)
- [`exists_point_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L38): Let a point be taken between `B` and `C`. (Points 3)
- [`exists_point_on_line`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L29): Let a point be taken on the straight line `L`. (Points 2)
- [`exists_point_on_line_off_line`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L34): Let a point be taken on `L`, not on the different straight line `M`. (Points 2, with "distinct from `M`")
- [`exists_point_opposite_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L46): Let a point be taken on the other side of `L` from `B`. (Points 6)
- [`exists_point_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L42): Let a point be taken on the same side of `L` as `B`. (Points 5)
- [`inside_not_on`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L38) (used here): A point inside a circle is not on it. (Generalities 4)
- [`inside_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L161) (used here): A circle is "convex": between two points on or inside it, every point is inside. (Circle 2)
- [`line_circle_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L69): A straight line through a point `B` inside a circle, heading out to a point `C` outside it, cuts the circle between `B` and `C`. (Intersections 4)
- [`line_circle_beyond`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L75) (used here): A straight line through a point `B` inside a circle, produced beyond `B` away from `C`, cuts the circle there. (Intersections 5)

- [`lines_meet_of_opposite_sides`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L179) (used here): A straight line joining points on opposite sides of `L` crosses `L`. (Intersection 1)

- [`not_on_line_of_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L92) (used here): Points on one side of a straight line are not on it. (Same side 3)
- [`on_line_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L56) (used here): A straight line through `A` and `B`, with `B` between `A` and `C`, passes through `C`. (Between 2)
- [`on_line_of_between_ends`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L61) (used here): A straight line through `A` and `C` passes through every point between them. (Between 3)
- [`pasch2`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L111) (used here): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, `A` is on `L` and `B` is off it, then `B` and `C` are on the same side of `L`: a straight line that leaves `L` at `A` does not cross it again. (Pasch 2)
- [`pasch3`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L114) (used here): A straight line through a point between `A` and `C` separates them. (Pasch 3)
- [`pasch4`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L119) (used here): If two different straight lines `L` and `M` meet at `B`, and `A` and `C` are points of `M`, different from each other and from `B`, that are not on the same side of `L`, then `B` is between `A` and `C`. (Pasch 4)
- [`same_side_or`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L99) (used here): A straight line has only two sides. (Same side 5)
- [`same_side_refl`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L85) (used here): A point off a straight line is on the same side of it as itself. (Same side 1)
- [`same_side_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L89) (used here): If `A` is on the same side of a straight line as `B`, then `B` is on the same side as `A`. (Same side 2)
- [`same_side_trans`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L96) (used here): Two points on the same side of a straight line as a third point are on the same side as each other. (Same side 4)
- [`triple_incidence1`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L131): Take `B` on `L`, `C` on `M` and `D` on `N`, three straight lines through `A`. If `C` lies within the angle `BAD` (on `D`'s side of `L` and on `B`'s side of `N`), then `B` and `D` are not on the same side of `M`: the straight line `AC` separates them. (Triple incidence 1)
- [`triple_incidence2`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L139): Take `B` on `L`, `C` on `M` and `D` on `N`, three straight lines through `A`, with `B` other than `A` and `D` off `M`. If `C` and `D` are on the same side of `L`, and `B` and `D` are not on the same side of `M`, then `B` and `C` are on the same side of `N`: `C` lies within the angle `BAD`. (Triple incidence 2)

**Lengths, angles and areas**

- [`adjacent_eq_of_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L67) (used here): A right angle is equal to the angle adjacent to it. (Diagram-angle 3; the other half is Definition 10 together with Postulate 4)
- [`angle_add_of_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L54) (used here): If `D` lies within the angle `BAC`, then `BAC` is made up of `BAD` and `DAC`. (Diagram-angle 2)
- [`angle_eq_of_same_rays`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L72) (used here): The angle doesn't change if its arms are traced through other points on the same rays. (Diagram-angle 4)
- [`angle_le_two_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L29): No angle exceeds two right angles. (Metric 5)
- [`angle_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L26) (used here): The angle `ABC` is the angle `CBA`. (Metric 4)
- [`area_add_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L88): Cutting a triangle in two from a vertex adds up. (Diagram-area 2)
- [`area_congruent`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L43): Triangles equal in all their sides and angles are equal in area. Euclid uses this without comment once he has shown two triangles congruent. (Metric 9)
- [`area_degenerate`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L32): A "triangle" with a repeated corner has no area. (Metric 6)
- [`area_eq_zero_of_on_line`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L80): A "triangle" whose corners lie on one straight line has no area. (Diagram-area 1)
- [`area_rotate`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L35): The triangle `ABC` is the triangle `CAB`. (Metric 8)
- [`area_swap`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L38): The triangle `ABC` is the triangle `ACB`. (Metric 8)
- [`eq_of_len_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L17): A finite straight line with distinct ends has length. (Metric 1)
- [`inside_of_len_lt`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L33) (used here): A point nearer the centre than the circumference is inside. (Diagram-segment 4)
- [`len_add_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L21) (used here): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, then `AB` and `BC` together make up `AC`. (Diagram-segment 1)
- [`len_lt_of_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L37): A point inside is nearer the centre than the circumference. (Diagram-segment 4)
- [`len_self`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L20): The "straight line" from a point to itself has no length. (Metric 1)
- [`len_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L23) (used here): The straight line `AB` is the straight line `BA`. (Metric 3)
- [`on_line_of_area_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L84): A triangle with no area has its corners on one straight line. (Diagram-area 1)
- [`same_ray_of_angle_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L49) (used here): If the angle `BAC` is nothing, `C` lies on the ray from `A` through `B`. (Diagram-angle 1)

**Superposition**

- [`superposition`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Superposition.lean#L30): **Superposition.** The triangle `ABC` can be applied to the straight line `L` with `A` on `D`, `B` on the ray from `D` through `G`, and `C` on the side of `L` where `H` is, without changing any side or angle.

**Laws of magnitude**

- [`add_assoc`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L23): Adding three magnitudes in a row, it makes no difference whether the first two or the last two are added first. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_comm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L26) (used here): The order of adding does not matter. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_lt_add_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L45) (used here): Adding the same thing to both sides keeps "less than". (System E §3.5)
- [`add_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L29): Adding nothing changes nothing. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_irrefl`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L32) (used here): No magnitude is less than itself. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trans`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L35) (used here): What is less than the less is less still. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trichotomy`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L39) (used here): Of two magnitudes, one is less, or they are equal, or the other is less. (System E §3.5)
- [`not_lt_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L42) (used here): Nothing is less than zero. (System E §3.5)

</details>

## Mishnah

**Move BC beside FG.** Euclid draws a new straight line MN as far from E as BC, so III.14 makes them equal, and at right angles to EK, so it lies beside FG, parallel to it. Two triangles with equal radii for sides now stand at E, and the greater angle MEN gives the greater base by I.24. The same MN settles the diameter's claim: AD is two radii, and two radii together exceed MN by I.20. Euclid gives no citation for cutting off EL equal to EH, or for drawing LM at right angles: they are I.3 and I.11.

**"Euclid himself assumes."** Heath sees the figure at work: "Euclid himself assumes that the angle subtended at the centre by MN is greater than the angle subtended by FG, or, in other words, that M, N both fall outside the triangle FEG" (vol. 2, p. 37), an assumption like those of III.7 and III.8. The reason is ready: "its truth is obvious because EM, EN, being radii of the circle, are greater than the distances from E to the points in which MN cuts EF, EG" (vol. 2, p. 37).

**Why can MN and FG never meet?** Lean wants Heath's reason in full, from one step back. Were they to meet, the triangle that point makes with L and K would have two right angles, against I.17; so F and G lie across MN from E. Each point where MN cuts EF or EG is then within the circle, and so between L and the end of MN on its side. `Prop15.half` makes one half of the angle comparison this way, and the two halves together are Euclid's MEN greater than FEG. Our statement gives E and the perpendiculars EH, EK, so there is no construction by III.1 or I.12 to repeat.

**Simson leaves MN out.** Robert Simson's proof compares instead the squares on the perpendiculars and on the halves of the straight lines, after a similar proof by Theodosius (*Sphaerica* I.6), and Simson adds the converse. Heath wonders whether Euclid "would have regarded this as too complicated an inference to make without explanation or without an increase in the number of his axioms" (vol. 2, p. 37). Euclid's MN keeps the comparison in the two triangles before us, but asks us to account for where their points fall.

**The modern way.** A straight line in a circle of radius r that subtends the angle θ at the centre has length 2r sin(θ/2), which grows with θ until θ is two right angles and the straight line is the diameter, 2r. That is Euclid's route: the nearer straight line subtends the greater angle, and I.24 does the rest.

## Further reading

- For how Greek astronomers tabulated the straight lines in a circle, where trigonometry began, Eli Maor's [*Trigonometric Delights*](https://press.princeton.edu/books/paperback/9780691202198/trigonometric-delights) (1998), ch. 2, a warm, story-filled history.
- For the place of this comparison in Book III, Benno Artmann's [*Euclid: The Creation of Mathematics*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-1412-0) (1999), the chapter "Euclid Book III: About the Circle", a mathematician's affectionate guide to the book.
